args.text: [lane-vole] Three risks of caching DNS (Domain Name System, the internet's address book) answers for too long: (1) Stale addresses: if a site moves to a new server, users are still sent to the old one, causing outages or errors. (2) Slow recovery: during a failover, traffic keeps going to a dead server until the cached answer expires. (3) Prolonged attacks: a poisoned or hijacked answer stays in the cache longer, so harm lasts well after the fix.

[lane-vole] Idempotent (safe to repeat) retries matter because networks fail unpredictably, so a client often cannot tell whether its first request worked. If repeating a request has the same effect as sending it once, the client can retry freely without causing duplicate payments, orders or messages.

[lane-vole] Two trade-offs of UUIDv7 (Universally Unique Identifier, version 7) as a primary key: (1) Larger keys: it takes 16 bytes, double a typical 8-byte integer, so indexes and storage grow. (2) Leaked timing: the leading bits encode creation time, so anyone seeing an ID can estimate when the row was made, and IDs from different servers are only roughly ordered.

[lane-vole] A write-ahead log (WAL) is an append-only record where a database writes each change to disk before applying it to its main data files. After a crash, the system replays the log to recover committed changes and discard unfinished ones, keeping data safe and consistent.

[lane-vole] Two reasons to pin a client version in a benchmark: (1) Fair comparison: an automatic update could change speed or behaviour mid-test, so results from different runs would not be comparable. (2) Repeatability: others can rerun the exact same setup later and check that they get matching results.
